messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: GGIR 1.2-10 online
parts:
GGIR version 1.2-10 is now online.

I have summarized the key updates here.

I felt the need to change the function argument for specifying bout calculation again. The underlying calculations are exactly the same though.

The original implementation from 2014 is still there (use bout.metric = 1 to get those). Earlier this year I thought the original 2014 implementation was inappropriate and so I added a new metric, being bout.metric 2. However, after thinking more about it I do not think that either one of them is truly superior; they are just different ways of quantifying a bout.

My impression is that there is not much literature on how to count a bout in the presence of epoch-level data with epoch lengths shorter than 1 minute. So, I implemented another metric (number 3) to allow myself to compare various options. I documented all three metrics and added function g.getbout. This function should enable the user to inspect my code for bout calculation, test it isolated from the rest of the package, and help identify what metric for calculating bouts is most sensible.

The challenge with designing a bout metric is that we need to decide how to account for breaks in bouts, how to account for the natural occurrence of values below or above a threshold because of the Gaussian nature of the data, and how to account for beliefs about what constitutes a physiologically meaningful bout of activity or inactivity: Do we allow someone to take a 10 second break? and how about a 1 minute break? Should the length of the maximum break length be proportional to the duration of the bout? Can there be activity bouts within a very long inactivity bout?

If anyone knows literature investigating this issue then I would appreciate hearing from you. If new bout metrics are to be added in the future then I will just number them 4, 5, ... So, in that way reproducibility of original calculations should be preserved regardless of whether we like them.

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: GGIR 1.2-10 online
parts:
Thanks to one of the package users I discovered today that I
accidentally introduced a bug in the code as part of my recent
modifications, which results in zero time in MVPA. I have no fixed
this and uploaded a new package version to the CRAN repository, which
should be online in the upcoming 24 hours pending their approval. The
new version number will be 1.2-11.
Vincent
